title: Advertising and Demand for Addictive Goods: The Effects of E-Cigarette Advertising
eligible_reason: Continuous treatment: the reduced-form border-county regressions (Table 4) regress weekly county sales of cigarettes, e-cigarettes, patches and gum on log e-cigarette and anti-smoking advertising GRPs with prices as controls and border-pair-by-week FE plus DMA-by-border FE; household regressions (Tables 5, 15) add lagged purchase indicators; the main analysis is a structural demand model. No binary staggered treatment.
design_notes: Package is a 7-zip archive (mksc.2019.1195.zip, identical to the _archive copy) containing an inner zip SandBox/ with Build/, Descriptive Regressions/, Model Estimation/ (Matlab BLP-type estimation) and Model Simulations/. Descriptive Regressions/2. BorderCountyRegs.do: areg cartridges/totpacks_cig lgrp_ecig_tot lgrp_anticig_tot price_* ppu_* i._dma_border, absorb(_week_border); excise-tax changes used only to drop observations (tax_change2/3 == 0). 4. AllCountiesRegs.do (Appendix Table 7) uses county and week FE with the same continuous ad regressors.
data_files_note: Constructed Nielsen (retail scanner, homescan, Ad Intel) county-week and household panels are shipped inside the nested archive (inspected by listing only after extracting the outer 7z layer to a scratch directory).
data_provenance_note: Constructed analysis files from licensed Nielsen data, shipped.
software_notes: Stata (build and descriptive regressions) and Matlab (structural model).
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally; table mapping from Descriptive Regressions/_Readme.rtf (Table 4 = border-county regressions, Tables 5/15 = household regressions, Table 7 in Appendix A = all-county regressions).
